c.h: 氵 is a component form of 水.

c.h: 衤 is a component form of 衣.

裡.o: Phonosemantic compound. 衤 represents the meaning and 里 represents the sound.

無.o: Pictograph of a person dancing, with ox tails or bird feathers hanging from his arms, to pray for rain. Original form of 舞 (dance). The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

次.o: The 二 (two) component represents the meaning "second" and also indicates the sound. The 欠 (deficient) represents the meaning "secondary" or "substandard".

the first time; first; number one
first; first time; for the first time

We promise to keep your information absolutely confidential.

c.h: Depicts a person opening their mouth to laugh.

歡.o: Phonosemantic compound. 欠 represents the meaning and 雚 represents the sound. 欠 (yawn) is a pictograph of a person with an open mouth, used here to represent a person joyfully laughing.

員.o: Depicts the round opening (口) of a cooking pot (鼎). Based on the original meaning "round", now written as 圓. The current meaning is a phonetic loan.

c.h: Shorthand for the 攸 component in the traditional character 條.

条.o: Simplified form of 條. Phonosemantic compound. 木 represents the meaning and 攸 represents the sound.

胡.o: Phonosemantic compound. ⺼ represents the meaning and 古 represents the sound. Based on the original meaning "flesh under the chin of a cow", which later shifted to "beard" (now written as 鬍 in traditional characters). Also used pejoratively to refer to foreigners from central Asia, who tended to have more beards than Han Chinese people. This meaning also shifted to "reckless" and "outrageous".
